evidence.quote: One of the problems posed in this paper is the following: Is \(\ell^ 1\)- ultrametrizable?
This has been solved by J. M. Bayod negatively when the base field is non-trivially valued, and this has appeared in the same volume in which this paper under review has appeared.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a non-trivially valued non-archimedean (complete) field, and let
$$\ell^1(K) = \Big\{ (x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} : x_n \in K, \ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |x_n| < \infty \Big\}$$
be the Banach space over $K$ equipped with the norm $\|(x_n)\|_1 = \sum_{n} |x_n|$. A norm $\|\cdot\|$ on a $K$-vector space $E$ is called an ultranorm (non-archimedean norm) if it satisfies the strong triangle inequality $\|x+y\| \le \max(\|x\|,\|y\|)$ for all $x,y \in E$. The space $\ell^1(K)$ is said to be ultrametrizable (as a topological vector space) if there exists an ultranorm on $\ell^1(K)$ that defines the same topology as the norm $\|\cdot\|_1$.

Question: Does there exist an ultranorm on $\ell^1(K)$ that is equivalent to the standard $\ell^1$-norm, i.e., is $\ell^1(K)$ ultrametrizable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered negatively by J. M. Bayod: when the base field is a non-trivially valued non-archimedean field, $\ell^1$ is not ultrametrizable. The resolution appeared in the same volume as the problem proposal.

status_evidence.title: Bayod, Productos internos en espacios normados no arquimedianos
status_evidence.snippet: Bayod showed that the ℓ^1 space over a non-trivially valued non-archimedean field does not admit an equivalent non-archimedean (ultrametric) norm.
status_evidence.claim: ℓ^1 is not ultrametrizable over a non-trivially valued non-archimedean base field.
